summary: Lisbon combines historic neighborhoods, riverfront viewpoints, and strong public transit for a compact city stay.
hotel_areas: Baixa and Chiado are central and convenient for first-time visitors.
Avenida da Liberdade offers larger hotels and direct metro access.
activities: Explore Alfama on foot and visit a miradouro.
Use a day for Belém and its riverfront monuments.
practical_guidance: Wear shoes suitable for steep cobbled streets.
Validate transit tickets before travel where required.

summary: Tokyo is best planned by grouping neighborhoods along convenient rail lines and allowing transfer time between districts.
hotel_areas: Shinjuku provides broad rail access and extensive evening dining.
Ueno is practical for museums, lower-cost lodging, and connections toward northern Tokyo.
activities: Pair Asakusa with Ueno for a traditional district and museum day.
Consider Kamakura or Nikko for a full-day trip after checking current transport schedules.
practical_guidance: Use a reloadable transit card for most urban rail and convenience-store purchases.
Confirm the last train when planning late evening activities.

summary: Mexico City rewards neighborhood-based planning because travel times vary significantly with traffic.
hotel_areas: Roma Norte and Condesa offer restaurants, parks, and walkable evening options.
Centro Histórico is convenient for major historic sites during the day.
activities: Visit the National Museum of Anthropology and Chapultepec Park together.
Reserve a separate half-day for the historic center and major murals.
practical_guidance: Allow extra transfer time during peak traffic.
Use official or app-based transportation options at night.
